text.p: The Guatemalan government fired 53 police investigators on Friday, including five police charged with kidnapping, the Interior Minister said.
"We are carrying out the firing of 53 members of the Criminal Investigations Department and also the arrest of five of them charged with kidnapping," Minister Rodolfo Mendoza told reporters.

Mendoza said an internal investigation had collected enough evidence to arrest the five detectives, including a high-ranking member of the force's elite anti-kidnapping unit, for the abduction of a young woman.
He did not say when or where she had been kidnapped.
According to Mendoza, the other 48 National Police officers were fired because an investigation determined they had handled cases incorrectly.

The firing was the third large-scale purge of allegedly corrupt police officers since President Alvaro Arzu took office just over a year ago. Army personnel and government officials have also been fired in large numbers since September.
